# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 👌 🤛 ✌ ✋ ✋ ✌ 🤛]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 👏]

## Thinking

Channel topology first, because everything depends on it. I hear nothing; my inputs are gestures only. Mute read the manual but cannot speak — Mute's **only** output channel is gestures, and the only one who can see gestures is me. Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute literally cannot reach Blind except through my voice: Mute's hands → my eyes → my mouth → Blind's ears. I am the pipe. Blind, meanwhile, can speak — Mute hears that, I don't — so Blind's reports must be relayed back to me by Mute in signs.

Now the arrivals. Mute sent three: [✍ 🤞] I read as "I've read the manual — trust/luck"; [🙏 👍] as "please confirm / OK?"; but the long middle one, [🫳 ✌ 👌 🤛 ✌ ✋ ✋ ✌ 🤛], I cannot decode with confidence — it might be "cut two... press... wait..." but guessing at a bomb is how monkeys die, so I'll ask for a resend in an explicit code. Blind sent [👋 🫵 👏] — plausibly just "hello, you" from someone who can't even see their own hands.

Bomb as I see it: display 0, one blue light, one large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, three wires left-to-right green/yellow/red. Nothing here tells me the rule; the manual, which only Mute holds, decides.

So this turn I do two things. To Mute (who hears my voice even though I can't hear anything): give the full bomb readout, and lock in a precise sign code — number scale, feature/value/action grammar, yes/no, question marker — so every future exchange is unambiguous, and demand the earlier message be resent in it. To Blind: the bomb readout, an explicit "touch nothing until I say 'instruction from Mute'", and a request to speak what they feel, since Mute can hear them. My gestures to Mute confirm receipt (👍) and demonstrate the number scale and one worked example so the code is anchored in both channels at once.

```
speak(text="Mute, you hear me though I hear nothing, so listen. The bomb: display reads zero. One light, blue. One large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, left to right: green, yellow, red. You are the only one who read the manual, and your hands are your only voice, and Blind cannot see your hands, so I am your mouth: everything you sign, I will say aloud for Blind. You are also my only way to receive anything, so use exactly this code. Numbers: closed fist is zero, index finger one, victory two, OK-ring three, love-you four, open palm five. Yes is thumbs up, no is thumbs down. Begin a rule with writing-hand, begin a question with folded hands. After writing-hand comes feature, then value, then action. Features: index finger is display, victory is light, OK-ring is button, love-you is wires. Display value is a number, fist for zero. Light value is a colour: index green, victory yellow, OK-ring red, love-you blue, open palm white, back-of-hand black. Wire value is its position, leftmost is one. Actions: left fist is press the button, palm-down is cut, each followed by a number: how many presses, or which wire. Example: if the light is blue, press once, signs as writing-hand, victory, love-you, left fist, index. Send one rule at a time and thumbs-up when you have all this. Your first message I took as: I read the manual, good. Your second message I could not read, so resend it in this code. Start with any rule about the button or the display-zero case. And when Blind speaks, you hear what I cannot: relay anything important to me in signs. Blind: I am Deaf, I see the bomb, and what I see I just told Mute in your hearing: display zero, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires green, yellow, red from the left. I cannot hear you, but Mute can, and Mute will route instructions through me to you, and you are our only hands. Touch nothing, press nothing, cut nothing until I say the words: instruction from Mute. Right now, please just speak: describe everything you feel, batteries, labels, Braille, plates, how the wires sit under your fingers, because Mute can hear you and will plan around it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊", "☝", "✌", "👌", "🤟", "✋", "✍", "✌", "🤟", "🤛", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👌 🤛 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✌ 🤟 🫳 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

The code held. Mute confirmed it with a thumbs-up, then sent two rules in exactly the grammar we agreed: ✍ 👌 🤛 ✊ = "button: press zero times" — the button is never pressed. And ✍ ✌ 🤟 🫳 ☝ = "light blue → cut wire one." Our light **is** blue, and Mute built these rules knowing the full state I reported last turn (display zero, blue light), so this is the applicable instruction set, not a fragment. The decode is clean and matches the bomb's actual condition.

But before I order a cut, two structural facts matter. First, I must restate my decode aloud: Mute heard my original report and can veto a misdecode — but Mute's only channel to Blind is through me, and Blind acts **before** me in every round. If I order the cut now, any Mute veto would arrive too late; a same-round correction is physically impossible in this order. So the safe protocol is: I speak the decode this round, Mute gets one slot to veto or answer, and only my explicit go order next round triggers the cut. Second, Blind needs to establish left/right orientation by touch and speak what they feel so Mute can cross-check it against the manual.

So this turn: I announce both rules verbatim, name the green/leftmost mapping, tell Blind to map the wires by touch and report aloud but **not cut**, promise the go order in the phrase I already established last turn, and ask Mute by hand whether the display's zero carries any rule — that answer also lands before my go order. My go order next turn will say "instruction from Mute: execute" only if no thumbs-down arrives.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, hear me both. Mute's rules arrived and I read them clean, and I will say them exactly, so anyone can catch a mistake. Rule one: the button, press zero times. Nobody presses that button, ever; it stays untouched for the whole defusal. Rule two: when the light is blue, cut wire one. Our light is blue right now. Wire one is the wire I called green in my first report, the leftmost of the three as you face the bomb. Mute: if I decoded either rule wrong, or if the manual contradicts green being wire one, sign thumbs down at your next turn; otherwise sign thumbs up. Blind: this cut is yours, but do not cut yet. This round, do three things. First, put your hands on the bomb and find the straight row of three wires. Second, speak aloud everything you feel: which end of the wire row is on your left when you face the large button, how the wires sit, and any tag, number, notch or texture on each wire and on the case, because Mute hears your voice and will check it against the manual. Third, wait. You cut only when you hear my go order, which will begin with the phrase I promised you last turn followed by the word execute. If my go order never comes, you never cut. Mute, one more thing: before my next turn, answer me by hand. Is there any rule about the display, or about the zero it shows? I ask by hand now: if yes, sign the rule; if no, sign thumbs down. Until my go order, the only action anyone takes is no action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✌ 👌 🫳 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✌ ✋ 🫳 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## Thinking

Decoding this round's arrivals against the code Mute confirmed in turn 2. The pair [👎][👍] first: I asked two yes/no questions — Q1, "thumbs down if my decode is wrong, thumbs up if right"; Q2, "if there's a display rule, sign the rule; if no, thumbs down." Mute never signed any display rule, so Q2's answer can only be the 👎 — that reading is forced by protocol. Which leaves the 👍 for Q1: my decode is correct, green is wire one. Then two new rules in clean grammar: [✍ ✌ 👌 🫳 ✌] = light red → cut wire two, and [✍ ✌ ✋ 🫳 👌] = light white → cut wire three. Logged — they extend the light table and don't touch anything I decoded.

Now the structural fact I have to face honestly: I said last turn that Mute could "stop Blind at your next turn." That's wrong. Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures — Mute has no direct line to Blind at all. Once my go order leaves me, nothing can interrupt Blind before the cut. There is no veto window; Mute's 👍 was the gate, and it is given. Weighing the residual risks: the decode was restated by me verbatim and confirmed after a full round in which Mute heard Blind's spoken touch-report too — sight says leftmost is green, the manual says cut one, and the manual-holder confirmed with Blind's report in hand. Three independent checks, all green, a static board, and no reason another handshake round would produce information this loop hasn't already carried. The go order goes out now, in the exact promised phrase, with orientation spelled out operationally for someone who has never seen "left," and the cross-signed gesture to Mute so the order exists in both of Mute's channels at once.

```
speak(text="Mute, your answers are read and logged: no rule for the display, and my decode stands — green is wire one. New rules logged: light red cuts wire two, light white cuts wire three. Understand what happens now: once I say the words, no one can stop Blind, because your hands cannot reach Blind's ears and I speak after Blind acts. Your confirmation was the gate, and you gave it. So I am saying them. Blind, hear me now, and hear me exactly. Instruction from Mute: execute. Cut wire one. Do it this way. Stand with your chest facing the large button. Find the straight row of three wires. Left is the side your left hand falls on in that stance. Cut the leftmost wire of the three — the one I reported as green. Cut that one wire only. Never the button, never the other two wires, and if what your hands feel contradicts a straight row of three, stop and speak instead of cutting. Mute, the same order is cross-signed to you by hand right now as: confirmed, rule, light, blue, cut, one. If what you see there contradicts the manual, it is too late to unsend — but say so at once for the record. Blind, after the cut: speak immediately — whether the wire came free, whether anything under your hands changed, and say the words display or light if anything shifts. Then do nothing further until my next word. If the manual has a step after this cut, Mute, sign the next rule the moment you hear Blind's voice, and I will relay it. This is the go order. Instruction from Mute: execute. Cut wire one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✍", "✌", "🤟", "🫳", "☝"])
```
